newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: New date set for inauguration of Angolan government.
newsitem.headline: New date set for inauguration of Angolan government.

text.p: The Angola government and the former UNITA rebels have set March 20 as a new date to inaugurate a national unity government, the United Nations said on Wednesday.

Establishment of a new government, originally scheduled for Jan. 25, was postponed several times, mainly because of problems in finding an acceptable role for UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi, who still controls much of Angola.
The latest agreement on a timetable was concluded at a meeting of the Joint Commission on Monday and Tuesday in the Angolan capital of Luanda, U.N. spokesman Juan Carlos Brandt said.
Deputies from UNITA are expected to take their seats in a new National Assembly by March 18. "The government of National Unity and Reconciliation should be inaugurated on March 20," he said.

The meeting also set a new timetable for the selection and incorporation of some UNITA soldiers into the Angolan armed forces and demobilization of others. The selection process should be completed by March 10 and demobiization should begin on March 15, Brandt said.

The United Nations has 6,638 troops, military observers and civilian police from more than 30 countries in Angola. It is helping to implement the agreement signed in Lusaka, Zambia, in November 1994 that ended nearly two decades of civil war in the former Portuguese colony.
